title: Pant Lost the Vice-Captaincy and the LSG Armband. His Coaches Say the Problem Is Not Leadership. It Is Shot Selection.
excerpt: Ryan ten Doeschate and childhood coach Devender Sharma say India's wicketkeeper must stop forcing horizontal shots and start playing to the match situation. The Afghanistan Test is his proving ground.
body:
Rishabh Pant arrived in New Chandigarh this week stripped of two leadership titles. The BCCI removed him as India's Test vice-captain when it announced the squad for Saturday's one-off Test against Afghanistan. Days earlier, he had voluntarily stepped away from the Lucknow Super Giants captaincy after the franchise finished last in IPL 2026.

Neither decision came without context. In India's most recent Test series — a 3-0 sweep by South Africa at home — Pant managed 49 runs in four innings at an average of 12.25. His IPL season was similarly lean. Across both formats, the swashbuckling innings that once defined him have been replaced by a pattern his own coaches now want addressed.

## "You Don't Need a Formal Title"

India's assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate, speaking to reporters in New Chandigarh on Thursday ahead of the Afghanistan Test, was direct about what the management expects.

"You don't need a formal title to become a leader," ten Doeschate said. "We need him to adjust his game to play according to the situation."

He confirmed that Pant had accepted the decision without complaint. "No complaints from Rishabh on being removed as vice-captain," the Dutch-born coach added.

KL Rahul, who has been appointed vice-captain for the Afghanistan Test, will partner Shubman Gill at the top of the leadership structure. It is a notable shift. Pant led India in Gill's absence during the Guwahati Test against South Africa — a match India lost by a record 408 runs.

## "He Is Pushing and Forcing Himself Too Much"

The advice from the Indian dressing room was echoed, independently, by the man who shaped Pant's game as a teenager. Devender Sharma, Pant's childhood coach in Delhi, told PTI on Thursday that the 28-year-old needs to return to basics.

"He is trying too much and mostly playing horizontal shots," Sharma said. "He is pushing and forcing himself too much. He should play more vertical shots — that will give him more success."

Sharma, who has coached Pant since the wicketkeeper was a boy at the Sonnet Club in Delhi, said the advice has already been delivered directly. "When I last talked to him, I had suggested him to play more vertical shots to get back into form. When you are not getting runs, you need to get back to basics."

But Sharma is not alarmed. He sees the lean patch as cyclical, not terminal.

"Rishabh is a mentally strong cricketer," he said. "After the car accident, when he went to England, he scored centuries in both innings of a Test match. It's a big thing for a cricketer. Ups and downs come in every cricketer's life. It's a phase and it will go."

## What the Numbers Show

Pant's Test record remains strong in aggregate: 3,476 runs in 49 matches at an average of 42.91. He has match-winning hundreds in England, South Africa, and Australia. The problem is recent form. Since his return from injury, the match-winning contributions have become less frequent, and the dismissals — often from expansive shots outside off stump — have become a pattern.

The IPL 2026 season offered no reset. Despite a lucrative contract with Lucknow, Pant struggled for consistency, and the franchise finished at the bottom of the table. His decision to step away from the captaincy was framed as a choice, but the timing told its own story.

## The Afghanistan Test as a Reset

Saturday's match at the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in New Chandigarh — the venue's first-ever Test — gives Pant a stage with lower stakes than the South Africa series but higher scrutiny. The Test falls outside the current World Test Championship cycle, but it sits squarely in the selection picture for India's tour of England later this summer.

Gill will captain a young squad that includes three potential debutants in left-arm spinners Manav Suthar and Harsh Dubey, and pace bowler Gurnoor Brar. Jasprit Bumrah has been rested. The batting order has room: Devdutt Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan are competing for the number three slot, and Dhruv Jurel is the backup wicketkeeper.

For Pant, the message from both the Indian camp and his first coach is the same. It is not about titles. It is about the next innings.

*Sources: PTI, Ryan ten Doeschate press conference (New Chandigarh, June 4), SportsTak, Times of India*
